topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space
target_audience: High school students or introductory undergraduate students

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space
outline.target_audience: High school students or introductory undergraduate students

sections.title: What is a Vector? (The Arrow Analogy)
sections.content: Introduce vectors as directed line segments representing both magnitude (length) and direction. Contrast them with scalars (simple numbers).
sections.example: A hiker moving 5km North: '5km' is the scalar magnitude, 'North' is the direction, and the arrow shows the displacement.

sections.title: Coordinate Representation (The Grid System)
sections.content: Explain how vectors are positioned on a Cartesian plane using [x, y] coordinates. Visualizing the vector as an arrow starting at the origin (0,0) and ending at point (x, y).
sections.example: A video game character jumping: The vector [3, 4] means moving 3 units right and 4 units up on the game screen.

sections.title: Vector Addition (The Tip-to-Tail Rule)
sections.content: Explain adding vectors visually. Place the 'tail' of the second vector at the 'tip' of the first. The resulting vector connects the starting point to the final destination.
sections.example: A boat crossing a river: One vector is the boat's speed, the other is the river's current. Combining them shows the boat's actual diagonal path.

sections.title: Scaling Vectors (Multiplication)
sections.content: Define scalar multiplication. Multiplying a vector by a number stretches or shrinks it. If the scalar is negative, the vector points in the opposite direction.
sections.example: A superhero 'Flash' running: If his speed vector is [2, 0], multiplying by 3 results in [6, 0]—a longer arrow representing higher speed.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Briefly recap how vectors form the backbone of graphics, physics, and AI. Emphasize that vectors are just 'instructions for movement' in a space.
sections.example: Connecting the concepts: Imagine a drone delivery path as a series of added vectors, mapped on a grid, scaled by wind speed, landing precisely at the target.

storyboard.title: What is a Vector? (The Arrow Analogy)
lecture_lines: Vectors show both magnitude and direction.
Scalars only describe simple numerical magnitude.
An arrow represents displacement in space.
animations: Draw an arrow vector in white color on the background.
Label the vector as 'v' in light blue (#00FFFF).
Highlight the tip of the vector by flashing yellow (#FFFF00).

storyboard.title: Coordinate Representation (The Grid System)
lecture_lines: Vectors live on a Cartesian grid.
Arrows start at the origin point.
animations: Draw a coordinate grid in light grey (#D3D3D3).
Place vector 'v' from origin to (2,3) in green (#00FF00).
Draw dashed lines to (2,0) and (0,3) in orange (#FFA500).

storyboard.title: Vector Addition (The Tip-to-Tail Rule)
lecture_lines: Connect the tail to the tip.
The result is the final path.
animations: Display two vectors 'v' and 'w' in white (#FFFFFF).
Move 'w' so its tail meets the tip of 'v'.
Draw the resultant vector 'v+w' in red (#FF0000).

storyboard.title: Scaling Vectors (Multiplication)
animations: Scale 'v' by factor 2, showing it grow longer.
Scale 'v' by factor -1, showing it reverse direction.

storyboard.title: Synthesis & Summary
animations: Display all vector concepts together in a summary layout.
Highlight vector addition with a gold glow (#FFD700).
Fade everything out to black (#000000) for conclusion.
